To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the combined action of IL‐12 plus IL-18 promotes monocyte differentiation into macrophage-like cells and induces the secretion of chemokines that recruit monocytes, activated CD4+ T cells and neutrophils.

IL‐12 and/or IL‐18, alone or in combination, promote the survival and differentiation of human blood and bronchoalveoar lavage (BALs) monocytes/macrophages and stimulate the production of chemotactic cytokines, including CXCL8, CXCL 9 and CXCL 10, that may regulate angiogenic responses.
IL‐12 and/or IL‐18, in combination or alone, promote the survival and differentiation of monocytes and macrophages, and induce the production of chemotactic CXC chemokines.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of IL12 and IL18 in the activation of the innate immune system, and the role of these cytokines in the resolution of inflammation.
the role of IL-12 and IL-18 in the activation of monocytes and macrophages and their potential impact in the resolution of inflammation.
the role of IL12 and IL18 in the regulation of monocyte/macrophage survival and function.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the combined action of IL‐12 plus IL-18 on monocytes and macrophages is a critical event for the regulation of the inflammatory response.
the combination of IL‐12 with IL‐18 induces the differentiation of monocytes into macrophages, which in turn produce chemokines that may regulate inflammation and angiogenesis.
IL‐12 and 18 are important cytokines for the survival of mononuclear phagocytes and the regulation of chemokine secretion.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
monocytes, in the presence of IL‐12 plus IL18, are activated and differentiate into macrophages and that mature macrophages, in the presence either of IL12 or IL18, produce chemokines.
IL‐12/IL‐18 may be involved in the regulation of the innate and the adaptive immunity in inflammatory processes.

IL‐12 and especially IL‐18 are important for the resolution of inflammation, as well as for the recruitment of mononuclear phagocytes, which may be important in the resolution of inflammation and in tissue repair.
The main takeaway from our work is that
IL‐12 and/or IL‐18 are key players in the inflammatory innate immune responses, by promoting monocyte survival and the production of chemotactic factors.
the cytokine IL‐18 is not just a proinflammatory cytokine, but can also be an important anti‐inflammatory cytokine.
IL‐12 and/or IL‐18 can induce the production of CCL2, CCL3 and CCL4 in monocytes and macrophages.
